title: Dizon orders MARINA, LTO to help in easing Port of Manila congestion
summary: Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon on Wednesday ordered the Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA) and the Land Transportation Office (LTO) to help in addressing the congestion issues hounding at the…

blocks.text: Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon on Wednesday ordered the Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA) and the Land Transportation Office (LTO) to help in addressing the congestion issues hounding at the Port of Manila.

“‘Yung port congestion natin ngayon sa Port of Manila dahil na rin sa global trade problems natin—madaming mga truck na nakabalagbag… by the way hindi lang 'yan maritime kundi LTO issue din 'yan,” Dizon said at a press conference.
(The port congestion now at the Port of Manila is due to global trade problems— there’s a lot of long queues of trucks… by the way this not just a maritime issue but also an LTO issue.)

“Maraming mga nagrereklamo sa ating mga truckers. Kailangan pagtulungan 'yan both ni Usec. Markus at ni Asec. Noreen,” the Transportation chief said, referring to newly-installed MARINA administrator Markus Lacanilao and LTO chief Noreen San Luis.
(A lot of truckers are complaining to us. This should be addressed by both Usec. Markus and Asec. Noreen.)

Last month, a “port holiday” was conducted against long queues and logistics issues at the Manila port, with consumer groups raising alarm over its consequences which could end up hurt consumers more.

Sought for comment, Alliance of Concerned Truck Owners and Organizations (ACTOO) vice president Rina Papa said, “Measures are being undertaken by both the private sector and several government agencies, we continue to push for a coordinated intervention at the national government level.”

“Port congestion goes beyond space and capacity within the ports. It is a complex, systemic issue involving local and national policies that cannot be adequately addressed by individual agencies with limited mandates,” Papa said.
She said ACTOO has already sought the intervention of Cabinet Secretary Benhur Abalos.
“We are hopeful that concrete measures will be underway before the peak of the holiday season,” she added.

Latest data from the BOC showed that overall yard utilization at Manila’s South Harbor stood at 74%, as of November 25, while the utilization rate for refrigerated container yards reached 81%. — RSJ, GMA News
